title: A study plan
hookLine: write what, when, and with whom
tomorrow: Saba turns eighty on Sunday. what does the Mishnah say eighty is for?

lines: YOU MAY NEVER HAVE FREE TIME.
cards: A brand-new planner on the first day of school, every page clean, every intention huge. A few weeks later, the pages are blank. A plan like that doesn't fail from lack of wanting.
It fails from someday. Hillel saw that coming. In Pirkei Avot he warns: don't say, when I have free time I'll study, because you may never have free time.

teach.b: Shammai, the sage so often named beside Hillel, gives the other half in the same book: make your Torah study a fixed thing. The Hebrew word is keva, set, regular, the opposite of whenever.
So a study plan doesn't need to be big. It needs three answers. What: one text, the portion, a page of Talmud, a Psalm, a book you chose for next year.
When: a time that already exists in your week, after dinner on Tuesdays, the train on Monday morning.
With whom: a chavruta, a study partner, a class, a cousin, or a parent at the kitchen table.
Everything from this week fits inside it. Plan to teach what you learn. Leave room in the margin for your own notes.
Keep a list of the questions left. Let doubt come to the table. Expect some sweetness.
And write the rest into the plan, too: Shabbat is in the calendar on purpose.
Something to tell a friend tonight: Pirkei Avot sets Hillel and Shammai side by side on this one: a plan beats someday.

how: Jewish learners often set a fixed study time, alone, with a chavruta (study partner) or in a class, following Shammai's teaching in Pirkei Avot to make Torah study a fixed practice.

games.why: Hillel: don't say when I have free time I'll study; you may never have free time. Shammai adds: make it fixed.

practice: Write three short lines. What: one text you'd like to keep learning. When: one time that already exists in your week.
With whom: one name, even if it's only your own. Read the three lines back once; that's the plan.

wordCard.voice: A study plan: what, when and with whom. Shammai's fixed time, against Hillel's warning about someday.

orig.note: Hebrew: fixed, set. Shammai's line in Avot: make your Torah keva.

carryVoice: Your line: a plan to keep learning, because free time may never come. That's the study stretch, done.

sources.ref: Mishnah Avot 2:4 (Hillel: say not, when I have leisure I will study; perhaps you will have no leisure)
